column1: ## 107 inputs the engine had never been tuned against (65 captured, 42
## reproduced; provenance in manifest.tsv), rated on round 3's criteria (which
## are round 2's), reused unchanged and frozen in CRITERIA.md, with the sha256
## of every input in SHA256SUMS, BEFORE the first input was run.
## Engine: the 2026-10-20 worktree (VERSION 2.1.0 plus the 2026-10-16 fix
## round, the 2026-10-20 engine-defect fixes and the 2026-10-20 quality gate;
##   PASS     everything present AND correctly structured
##   PARTIAL  broadly right; something lost or mis-shaped
##   FAIL     the output misrepresents the input
## strategy/conf  the default-mode winner (--max-strategies 1, confidence rank)
## cov            its line coverage (%), the 4th field of --emit-meta
## cons           its column-type consistency (%), the 5th field of --emit-meta
##                ("-" when no column could be judged)
## gate_held      yes = provost's quality gate would hold this capture for
##                triage instead of filing it: the winner is a generic parser
##                json-array, jsonl, yaml, xml, toml, har; provost
##                Every held input here is held for coverage; no winner read
##                under 70 on consistency. No input was no-match or under the
## rating         default mode, judged on the melted tidy table (NAME.tidy)
## multi_datasets the number of datasets `provost --multi` files (NAME.multi)
## multi_rating   the --multi output rated on the same scale, each dataset
##                melted (NAME.multi.tidy) and the set judged as a whole; 57
##                inputs give one dataset byte-identical to the default table,
##                so the rating is the same
## note           one-line reason; where --multi differs it is described after
## The --rank priority winner differs from the default on 9 inputs (014, 018,
## 028, 045, 050, 058, 134, 135, 139); priority mode was recorded, not rated.

column13: note
indented-colon-groups keeps only the two "label:" lists (cov 28); every Inst/Conf record and the counts line are dropped; --multi is the same
nested derivations flattened into one wide record whose column names are built from content (calc.y_2, Shift_derivation.`->_10 ...); --multi the same

sections flattened: every grammar, symbol and conflict line becomes a column repeated on each State row (cov 67); --multi keeps every line in 31 datasets but shreds them word-per-column and promotes a record to header in two

text-lines fallback: every line kept, but code frames, carets, Expected/Received and (fail) lines are separate rows, no test records; --multi pulls one Expected/Received pair into its own table, the rest stays line-per-row
text-lines fallback keeps every line; key and value never split, sub-keys never tied to their parent; --multi splits two-word keys (Full / Path) across columns
the "Dumping total:" banner is the header; each tree line is cut at the first gap, so the connector glyphs and node text sit under "Dumping" / "total:" and depth is lost
the first report title is the header ("Pass execution timing report"); every timing row is cut into four arbitrary columns under those words, and the report titles and column headers become data rows

protobuf-text flattens the whole dump into one record, column names from content (|-FieldDecl_0x55a8...), the layout tables lost (cov 83); --multi keeps each layout as its own dataset, mostly line-per-row, one shredded word-per-column

key-value splits only the two lines whose command follows "):  " at the first colon; the other 45 trace and status lines sit whole in the key column with an empty value, so file, line and command are never separate fields; every line kept

help-columns: each option and command is one row with section, name and description; only ASCII-art banner lines are lost; --multi gives the same rows split into Options and Available commands datasets
indent-tree gives depth / name / parent for every flag, exactly the hierarchy; the three legend lines are depth-0 rows; --multi splits the legend into its own key/value dataset

a "# Terminal filters" comment heading becomes the header of the whole database, so keywords and values sit under "Terminal" / "filters"; every comment paragraph and section heading is dropped (60 rows from 100 lines); --multi keeps comments and sections apart, but promotes the first TERM entry to a header and labels colour codes name / description (pkg-config)

the key/value header is exact, but the histogram is read as key/value too: the header row and each extent row keep their counts glued in one value cell; --multi also shreds "Min. free extent:" word by word

kv-report keeps every key with its value, but the charset block is keyed inconsistently (charset, then the block offset), and the stray "(s)" line after it becomes the section label of the last 17 attributes
text-lines fallback keeps every line, but count, line number and source are never split and the function/branch annotations are rows of their own

block-records keeps the percentages but drops every record's identity: no function or file name survives, nor the Creating / No calls lines (cov 56); --multi drops the function names too and makes each file name a column header over word-split rows

grouped-rows promotes the "local path:" line into the column names, splits two-word keys across columns ("display" / "name:"), and loses name, type, size and uri from the top block; the attributes keep key and value only as separate word columns

line-records gives one row per command line with arguments word-split into A..S; heredoc bodies and EOF markers are rows like commands; every line kept; --multi takes the "# import config" comment as the header of every command row
text-lines fallback keeps every line, but declarations and their wrapped descriptions are separate rows and the TYPES heading is a row
yaml reads the list as one mapping: a single wide record with one column per linter, and the Enabled / Disabled group titles (the point of the output) are dropped
text-lines fallback: every line kept, but file:line:col, message and linter are never split, source and caret lines are rows of their own, and the per-linter counts are not a table

embedded-table keeps the flat profile (header row 1 merged away, names time/seconds/seconds_2) and drops the call graph and index entirely (cov 60); --multi keeps every section but puts the call-graph values under the wrong columns
kv-pairs keeps every string capability under its own name, but each wrapped source line becomes a sparse row, and the entry's names line, the boolean flags and the numeric caps are dropped (cov 79)
text-lines fallback: every line kept, but the [uptime][level][tags] prefix and GC(n) id are never split from the message
key-value glues each method's whole bytecode listing into one Code cell, drops the class line and the first member, and splits each member from its descriptor across rows

block-records merges the report into sparse rows keyed by labels, and drops the per-size chunk freelists (cov 77); --multi keeps every section as its own dataset, but promotes the first size class of each freelist to a header and flattens the usage rows into one wide record
brace-groups keeps every line under its event type, but "key = value" is never split, each event is spread over one row per field with no event id, and stack frames are rows like fields

the event table is exact with its real column names, and the Version / Chunks / Start / Duration header is carried on every row; --multi takes the table's header line as a value of the key/value block and leaves the table with positional names

block-records collapses the report into two sparse rows with duplicated names (regions, regions_2 ...), dropping the attach narration, GC type, generation titles and "% used" lines (cov 62); --multi keeps every line, the narration labelled name / description and the settings split around "="

help-columns gets most plugins right, but options printed on their own line land with an empty name and the option glued to the description, one option's sub-items become rows of their own, and a sentence from a description becomes the section label of the last plugins

block-records turns thread header text into column names ("main"_#1_[20910]_prio ...) and keeps one sparse row per thread; every stack frame is dropped (cov 40); --multi keeps every line, one dataset per thread group, but line-per-row or word-split

both lists come out exactly as group / name / description rows; only the two-line usage footer ("Use +feature to enable ...") is dropped; --multi drops the group names and splits the CPU descriptions word by word

the first echoed "(lldb) target create" command is the header; every later line is cut into three word columns plus a remainder under "(lldb)" / "target" / "create", mixing commands, source lines, frames and struct fields

tsv splits each attribute from its value at the tab, but DIEs are rows with an empty value, each DIE is spread over its attribute rows with no parent id, nesting depth is lost and the quotes in string values are stripped; --multi splits values word by word

text-lines fallback keeps every line, but neither the key/value summary nor the three bracket-numbered tables are split; --multi gets the summary exactly and the pressure row right, but leaves the [n] headers as data rows, shifts the MayStore mark one column and names the resource index "timestamp"

protobuf-text flattens the nested dump into one wide record with real dotted names (ElfHeader1.Ident1.Magic, Section3.Name ...) and right values, but the sections are columns rather than rows and every Flags [ ... ] list is dropped (cov 81)

the "ninja: Entering directory" line is the header; progress lines, the stats table (its own header a data row) and the hash-load footer are cut into word columns under "ninja:" / "Entering" / "directory"

bracket-log gives one row per GC event, but the [pid:isolate] tag is labelled timestamp, the elapsed ms and every measure stay inside message, and the program's own output line is attached as detail of the event before it
sequence label and op text are split cleanly, but the first op is promoted to the header, the "syntax OK" line is dropped and the indentation that encodes the op tree is lost
text-lines fallback keeps every line; none of the four method / ops/sec / usecs/op tables is split and the section titles are rows; --multi separates the sections but shreds one title word by word
the histogram values are right under positional names A/B/C, but its header row ("< us  % of total  count") is a data row and the narration lines are cut into word columns above it

indent-tree keeps the reflection nesting as depth / parent, but every closing brace is a node of its own and the bracketed descriptors are never split into kind / name / type; --multi fragments the class into line-per-row pieces
one row per diagnostic and the summary kept, but message, line and file are never split into columns

headerless tsv: all nine fields of every setting under honest positional names, empty cells kept; but double quotes inside the description texts are stripped ("archive_library" becomes archive_library)

tsv takes the first line's tab-separated pairs as the header ("Process:_sleep________", "State:_S_(sleeping)"), so every later "Key: value" pair sits whole under those names; no key is split from its value; --multi does the same for the first block, but reads the rest as key/value (second pair on a line left glued)
indent-tree ties each line to its man-style heading, but wrapped prose is one row per physical line and functions and data are not split from their descriptions
text-lines fallback keeps every line, but each formatter's names and its description are separate rows

embedded-table keeps only the five assertion lines of the one failure (cov 23), under a header made from a source line, with its words reordered; the session header, outcomes, captured output and summary are lost; --multi keeps them but labels the test-name rule "flags / path" (git-annex-list) and repeats the source-line header
indent-tree keeps the AST nesting as depth / parent, but field=value is never split and closing brackets stay glued to the last child

indented-hierarchy flattens the three tracebacks into one record: exception names become columns, one column name is built from a frame line, and almost every File/source frame and both chaining sentences are dropped (cov 83)
text-lines fallback keeps every line; offset, opcode byte, name and argument are never split, and the MARK nesting carried by indentation is lost

kind and name are split under positional names, but a class's bases are glued to its line number while methods have the line number in that column, and method-to-class membership (indentation) is lost

prefix-message gives one row per warning with file, line, message and the source line as detail; the warning category stays inside message, and the trailing tracemalloc hint is glued into one warning's detail
the listing is exact: names with spaces and the (already mis-decoded) non-ASCII name in File_Name, date and time together in Modified, sizes right-aligned

text-lines fallback keeps every line; progress percent, key type, key and size are never split and the summary sentences are rows; --multi splits the percent off (labelled timestamp) and keeps the rest line-per-row
every sample row exact under its real column names; the grouped data / load / child header line is kept as a title column on each row

text-lines fallback keeps every line; offset, instruction, operands and line marker are never split and the disasm headers are rows; --multi gives each ISeq a table with its header as title and splits offset / instruction / operands, but cuts the (line)[flags] marker in two on some rows
kv-report splits each line at its first "=", so "speed 38400 baud; rows 0; columns 0; line" is a key and "^C; quit = ^\; erase = ..." the value of intr; the flag words are values with no key

one row per syscall and group heading, but the heading and its members are not linked and each description is shredded word-per-column; --multi separates every heading, description and member list into 24 datasets, losing membership entirely

one row per override, but the [EXTENDED] type is labelled timestamp, the two paths are not split at the arrow, and the count footer is glued into the last row's detail; --multi keeps the footer apart but word-split
option / value split is right for every line, but the first option (activity-action other) is promoted to the header, so it is lost as a row and names both columns
the tool banner line is the header ("==22491==" / "Helgrind," / "a" ...); every report line is cut into word columns under those words, race blocks and stack frames are not records

the "times in msec" legend is the header; its two legend lines become data, and rows with three numbers put the third number glued to the event text while two-number rows put the event in that column, so events and times are under the wrong names

indent-tree keeps the DOM nesting below the document, but the document's own properties are depth-0 siblings, so the comment and root element get "standalone=true" as their parent; content= values are not split

offset / field / value rows are right under positional use, but the first record (0000 LOCAL HEADER #1) is promoted to the header, hex and decoded values stay glued, and the nesting of extra-field sub-entries is lost
exact: real column names, packed timestamps intact, multi-word descriptions whole in the last column
the description and settable columns are right, but attribute name and value are glued into one cell (the 16-character name column has no gap before long values)
one record with every padded key as a column and every value with its unit, END APC included

the table is exact under its real names, but the total footer becomes a data row spread across Vlan / Mac_Address / Type / Ports and the trailing prompt is a row; --multi loses the header (positional names, header line as data)
the echoed prompt "core-rtr1#show processes cpu sorted" is the header; the CPU summary and the real header row are data, and each process row is cut into four columns under the prompt's words

embedded-table keeps only the three members' traffic tables merged into one with no member name (cov 44); the pool status, pool traffic and member status blocks are dropped; --multi keeps every block as its own dataset, members as separate one-line datasets not linked to their tables
the echoed "SQL> SHOW TABLE KUNDEN;" prompt is the header; column definitions, continuation lines, constraints and triggers are cut into word columns under "SQL>" / "SHOW" / "TABLE" / "KUNDEN;"

block-records builds column names from log lines (on_docker-runner-03_..., E_______AssertionError) and keeps one sparse row per section; most log lines, the test output and the summary are dropped (cov 56); --multi uses each section's title sentence as the header of its log lines

block-records builds column names from the controller, array and drive lines (Smart_Array_P440ar_in_Slot_0_..., physicaldrive_1I_2) and drops the drive cages and all three logical drives (cov 65); --multi keeps every line as small word-split datasets, hierarchy lost

vertical-line slices at fixed character positions, so values from rows with a long H/W path are cut mid-word (CLAI / MED, DEVI / CE) and the device-file lines are chopped into fragments; --multi keeps whole words but shifts every value one column left of its header and splits the description across H/W_2 / Type

block-records turns each job row's leading words into a column name (mkrause__ID, lfischer_DAG ...) with the rest of the row as one value; --multi reads the table exactly with real names, but drops the Schedd banner and labels the two totals name / description
text-lines fallback keeps every line; the legend is not read as key/value and the interface table is never split into columns

block-records makes dot-leader labels into column names with the right-hand pair glued into each value, and drops the whole pool table (cov 42); --multi reads the pool table but shifts values one column off their grouped headers (Reserved size under Pool_(M), Max Active under Reserved_Size)

section-tables gives both tables one table with a section column and real names, banner and notes kept; but the "N active, M maximum" footers sit as rows under address / number, chunk and dbs stay glued in chunk/dbs, and the metadata continuation row lands under the wrong columns

aligned-columns reads all five tables as one under the Model table's header, so App, Unit, Machine and Offer rows sit under Model / Controller / Cloud/Region ..., their own headers are data rows and telegraf's empty Version shifts its row

indented-hierarchy keeps one interface's address continuation lines as a two-column record whose names are built from the row text; every other interface is dropped (cov 69); --multi the same plus the prompt lines
prefix-message splits every klog line into severity, timestamp, pid, file, line and message, and attaches the multi-line err=< ... > block to its event as detail
text-lines fallback keeps every line, but none of the three titled tab tables is split into columns
headerless tsv: all six fields of every taxon under honest positional names, the name keeps its leading spaces so the depth of the tree survives

every Key: value pair exact, including keys with parentheses and slashes and values with parenthesised byte counts; the one prose line is kept as a key with an empty value; --multi splits the blank-separated groups into datasets
text-lines fallback keeps every node line with its class attributes, but leading indentation is trimmed, so depth survives only where | rails remain; name, class and attributes are never split

equals reads one record, but every multi-line ( ... ) array becomes the value "(" with its items dropped (authors, type tree, used dates, where-froms; cov 83), and the padded keys keep runs of underscores
text-lines fallback keeps every entry, but the == section == titles are dropped, so device types, runtimes, devices and pairs run together; name, UUID and state are never split

the prompt and the flags legend are merged into the header ("Flags:", "[admin@MikroTik-Lager]_-", "dynamic," ...); key=value pairs are never split and wrapped lines and ;;; comments are separate rows under those names; --multi keys records 1-5 by name=value (dates and times split apart) but leaves the first record under the legend header

vertical-line slices at fixed character positions, cutting values mid-word (RECOVERY WRI / TER, CONTOSO\svc_repor / ting, 09:2 / 8:13 ...); the two SPID columns and REQUESTID survive; --multi keeps whole words but splits two-word cells and shifts the later columns
the echoed prompt is the header; both header lines are data, and each two-line session is two rows cut into columns under "admin@PA-3220>" / "show" / "session" / "all"

the metrics table is exact with all 34 real column names and empty trailing cells, but the comment header (the command line, start time and METRICS CLASS) is dropped; --multi keeps the comments as their own datasets and the table exact

csv splits at the comma after the severity letter and takes the first log line as the header, so every line sits under a column named after the first request; the Parameters hashes are cut at their inner commas and the backtrace lines land in the severity column
exact: real names, the dash rule dropped, the global row and every "-" placeholder kept in place

text-lines fallback keeps every line, but none of the three result sets is split into columns; --multi word-splits the first row under name / version (version-line) and leaves the other sets positional and word-split
bracket-log gives one row per line with the time split off, but the W:/E: status, the [Step n/m] block and the ##teamcity service-message attributes all stay inside message

kv-pairs reads the |-separated client list as one record: later clients become cid_2, client_nickname_2 ..., each client's clid is glued into the previous client_type ("1|clid=4"), and the error id=0 msg=ok status line is dropped (cov 50)

vertical-line keeps only the result table (cov 47): the null row's sales_amt is cut mid-number (88102.6 / 0) and the logoff lines below are chopped at the same character positions; the banner, logon status, query and row-count lines are dropped; --multi keeps every part, the table positional and with two-word cells split, its header line left in the dataset before it

the "Windows Boot Manager" title is the header; the later block titles are rows like settings, and descriptions with spaces are split across the title's columns; --multi gives each block its own dataset with the continuation value joined, but promotes each block's first setting (identifier) to its header

kv-report reads the banner, the RSOP block, both settings blocks and the filtered-GPO sub-blocks; but the applied-GPO and security-group lists are labelled by their own sub-heading only, so the computer's and the user's lists cannot be told apart

the empty SESSIONNAME cells shift those rows one column left (ID under SESSIONNAME, state under ID ...), and the two-word headers IDLE TIME and LOGON TIME are split into IDLE / TIME / LOGON, so idle time sits under TIME and dates under it

embedded-table keeps only the end-of-job summary table (cov 20); the job header, every per-file line, the error/retry lines and the speed footer are dropped; --multi keeps all of them, the header as key/value and file lines line-per-row, but glues each summary row's six counts into one cell

key-value keeps every pair, but the three task blocks run together as one long list with no task id, keys containing colons are split wrongly (Repeat / "Every: Disabled") and one key swallows its value ("Stop Task If Runs X Hours and X Mins: 72:00:00")

the gutter grid handles every multi-word cell, thousands separators and non-ASCII title, but CPU Time and Window Title are merged into one column (header and values), because the CPU Time values run up to the next column
exact: three real columns, multi-word descriptions whole; only the decorative PRIVILEGES INFORMATION title and rules are dropped

every connection row is right under positional names, but the #fields header (which names every column) is not applied, the #types line is a data row, the #path/#open metadata is dropped and #close is a row; --multi keeps the metadata as text but still leaves the table unnamed

the IDCAMS page header line is the header (IDCAMS / SYSTEM / SERVICES / TIME: ...); entry lines, KEY----value groups and the totals are cut into word columns under those words, and the carriage-control digit stays glued to entry types (0CLUSTER)
